LanguageData.RR_CannotBearRazor: {PAWN_nameDef} is not of Gold, and {PAWN_possessive} ideoligion forbids any lesser Color to bear a razor.
LanguageData.RR_CannotWearCasteArmor: {PAWN_nameDef} holds no title and is not of Gold, and {PAWN_possessive} ideoligion reserves recoil plate for those the hierarchy has decided to trust.
LanguageData.RR_CannotHoldServiceTitle: {PAWN_nameDef} is of Gold. The service ladder is what the Society offers those it will never raise, and {TITLE} is not a rank a Gold may hold.
LanguageData.RR_CannotConceiveAcrossColors: {PAWN1_nameDef} and {PAWN2_nameDef} are different Colors. The castes were engineered too far apart to interbreed; only a Carver could bridge it.
LanguageData.RR_Setting_SuppressXenotypesTip: Stops hussars, genies, neanderthals, impids, wasters, yttakin, pigskins, dirtmoles and highmates being generated, in factions and among wanderers alike, so new pawns read as Colors or as baseliners. The xenotypes themselves are untouched: existing pawns keep theirs, and they can still be built in a gene assembler.
LanguageData.RR_Setting_SuppressFactionsTip: Removes the generic outlander, tribal and pirate factions from the default world, leaving the planet to the Society and its rivals. Hidden factions, the ancients and the Empire are left alone. Nothing is deleted, so you can still add any of them back by hand on the world creation page.
LanguageData.RR_Setting_SuppressNote: These affect world generation only. Changing them will not alter a world that already exists - start a new one to see the difference.
LanguageData.RR_CannotHoldGoldTitle: {PAWN_nameDef} is not of Gold. The standing of {TITLE} is conferred by the Institute, and the Institute does not admit lesser Colors.
LanguageData.RR_Setting_AllowCarvingTip: Adds surgeries that rebuild a person into another Color directly, at great expense. Turn this off to keep carving as it is in vanilla Biotech - assembling a xenogerm at a gene assembler, which for a Gold means twenty-two gene processors and archite genes bought from traders. Switching this off removes a shortcut, not a capability.
LanguageData.RR_CarvingComplete: {PAWN_nameDef} has been carved. The registries will record {PAWN_objective} as {COLOR}.
LanguageData.RR_GravLaunchDesc: Ride the boots' field up out of the map and set down somewhere else on the planet, up to {0} tiles away. Anyone launching alone arrives alone, and arrives as a caravan on open ground rather than inside a settlement.
LanguageData.RR_GravLaunchCooldown: The boots are still bleeding off charge: {0} remaining.
LanguageData.RR_GravFlightArrived: The grav flight has come down.
LanguageData.RR_StatTraumaSuiteDesc:
The suit injects a stimulant on its own when the wearer starts bleeding badly or is in serious pain, and will not dose again until the last one wears off. It synthesises a replacement dose every {0}.
The suit also seals wounds continuously while worn, which is a separate effect and does not run out.
LanguageData.RR_RoleRequirement_AnyColor: Must be of a specific Color
LanguageData.RR_Setting_WidenFloorTip: Lowers the minimum total metabolism a xenogerm may have from -5 to -10, which several Colors need to be assemblable at all. This is a global tuning change: every gene assembler dialog in your game sees the new floor, including other mods'. Turn it off to restore the vanilla -5; takes effect immediately.
LanguageData.RR_RazorTrialGoldOnly: {PAWN_nameDef} is not Gold. A trial by razor is fought between Golds.
LanguageData.RR_ScenPartSigilsTrue: Colonists carry the sigil of their true Color.
LanguageData.RR_LurcherHuntText: Lurchers have come. The Society's hunters do not raid for loot; they have been sent for someone in your colony.
LanguageData.RR_LurcherHuntTextNamed: Lurchers have come for {PAWN_nameDef}. The Society's hunters do not raid for loot, and they know what {PAWN_pronoun} really is.
LanguageData.RR_CensusDiscrepancyText:
The census-takers of {0} have checked the hands of your colonists against the registry, and the paper does not match the person: {1}.
They have written it down. Goodwill lost: {2}.
LanguageData.RR_ScenPartCampaign: A story unfolds in acts. Its turning points are offers you may refuse.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_QuotaText:
The notice has come, on the same grey paper as every quarter.
The clan's quota is {0} canisters of helium-3, due in {1} days. The clan that beats its quota wins the Laurel: rations, quarters, the Society's regard.
The seam runs under the rig. The rig needs someone at its controls and wood in its generator. Whatever helium-3 is on your claim when the tithe-men come will be counted.
Everyone says this is the quarter. Everyone has said it before.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_QuotaMetText:
The tithe-men counted {0} canisters, wrote the number down, and loaded every one of them.
Then they read out the award. The Laurel has gone to another clan - one that mined less than yours did, and that the overseers find easier to deal with. It was decided before the quarter began. It is always decided before the quarter begins.
The clan dug until its hands split, met the number, and has been told that meeting it was never the point. People are saying so, loudly, where the tithe-men can hear.
That will be remembered. So will who said it.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_QuotaShortText:
The tithe-men counted {0} canisters against a quota of {1}, and took all of them.
The Laurel has gone to another clan. It would have gone to another clan regardless - the older Reds say it is decided before the quarter begins - but a shortfall is a different matter. A shortfall is written down as idleness, and the Society has a procedure for idleness.
Nobody has said what the procedure is. Everybody seems to know.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_ReprisalText:
The clan complained about the Laurel, and somebody wrote the complaint down.
A detachment of Grays is coming up the road to explain, in the only language the Society uses with Reds, that the award was fair. They have not come to count canisters. They have come to be seen doing it.
After today the Society will not be a distant thing that sends paper. It will be an enemy, because it has decided that you are one.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_ReprisalTextShort:
The shortfall has been assessed, and the assessment is arriving on foot.
A detachment of Grays is coming up the road to correct the clan's idleness. Nobody on the claim was idle. That has never been the kind of fact that matters.
After today the Society will not be a distant thing that sends paper. It will be an enemy, because it has decided that you are one.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_ContactText:
A stranger was waiting at the edge of the claim after the fighting. No sigil showing. Hands like yours.
The message is short. There are people who watched what the Society did here, and they are called the Sons of Ares, and they have someone who needs to disappear for a while - hurt, hunted, and worth more to the Society dead than your whole clan is worth alive. They will drop this person at your door if you say yes.
They are honest about the price. Whoever comes looking will come looking here.
If you refuse, they will not ask twice, and the clan's life goes on as it was.
Accept: the stranger arrives, wounded, and the story continues. Refuse: the story ends here. Your colony plays on as an ordinary one.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_DeclinedText:
The stranger nodded, as though it were the answer most people give, and walked back the way they had come.
Nobody will ask again. Whatever was going to begin here will begin somewhere else, with someone else's clan, or not at all.
The claim is quiet. The rig is still warm.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_HeroText:
A pod has come down hard near the claim, and {PAWN_nameDef} is in it - wounded, unconscious, and nothing like what the message led you to expect.
The build is a Gold's: the height, the bones, the eyes. A razor is strapped to {PAWN_possessive} arm. But the sigil on {PAWN_possessive} hand is a Red's, and the calluses under it are a helldiver's.
Someone took a Red apart and carved a Gold out of the pieces. The Society believes that cannot be done. It is the reason {PAWN_nameDef} is worth hiding, and the reason hiding {PAWN_objective} will not work for long: a hand that says Red on a body that says Gold is exactly what the Lurchers are sent to find.
Get {PAWN_objective} to a bed.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_Wave1Text:
Word of what happened to the Lurchers has travelled faster than anyone can explain.
Two Obsidians are at the edge of the claim. They were bred to believe Golds are gods, and they have just learned that hunters sent by gods can be beaten by miners. The Sons of Ares cut their collars a month ago and have had nowhere to send them since.
They are not asking for much. They are asking whether it is true.
Accept: two freed Obsidians join the colony. Refuse: they move on. The story continues either way.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_Wave2Text:
The garrison that marched on you did not all march home, and not all of the missing are dead.
Two Grays have walked in with their rifles reversed, and an Orange who kept the garrison's machines running has come with them, carrying most of a toolkit that is not theirs. They were ordered to burn a mining clan and found they would rather not.
The Sons of Ares vouch for them. A Gray who changes sides once is a risk. A colony that turns away rifles before what is coming is a bigger one.
Accept: two Gray defectors and an Orange saboteur join the colony. Refuse: they go on to the Sons of Ares. The story continues either way.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_RecruitsText: They have come in from the edge of the claim: {0} more for the colony ({1}). They are yours now, and so is whatever follows them.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_GarrisonText:
A mining clan has killed the Society's hunters and is sheltering something the Society wants. That is no longer a matter for a detachment.
The district garrison has been turned out in strength. Their orders are not to punish the claim. Their orders are to end it.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_RainWarningText:
The Sons of Ares have sent one line, and it is not an offer.
A Society warship has taken up station above the claim. A garrison was lost here; that is now a Gold's embarrassment, and Golds settle embarrassments personally. They will not march. They will come down from orbit, onto your roofs, in about {0} days.
They call it an Iron Rain. No colony of lowColors has ever been worth one before.
Build what you can. Arm everyone. This is the last thing they have to throw.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_RainText:
The sky is full of falling steel.
This is an Iron Rain: the Society coming down out of orbit onto the heads of people it has decided must not exist. There is no line to hold and no road to watch. They are landing among you.
Everything the clan has done since the quota comes down to this hour.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_WonText:
The last of them is down, and the ship above the claim has gone.
It will be reported as a withdrawal. Everyone who matters will know what it was: the Society dropped its best onto a mining clan, and the mining clan is still here. {PAWN_nameDef} is still here. A thing the Golds said could not be made, standing in the wreckage of the thing they said could not be stopped.
There will be other clans. Some of them are already asking how it was done.
The Rain is over. What the claim becomes now is still to be settled.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_WonTextNoHero:
The last of them is down, and the ship above the claim has gone.
It will be reported as a withdrawal. Everyone who matters will know what it was: the Society dropped its best onto a mining clan, and the mining clan is still here. The stranger they came for did not live to see it. It turns out not to have depended on one person after all.
There will be other clans. Some of them are already asking how it was done.
The Rain is over. What the claim becomes now is still to be settled.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_ClansText:
The Rain was seen from three claims away, and so was the morning after it.
Two Reds have walked in from the next seam along. Their clan could not spare them and sent them anyway, with a pod of what it could gather: rations, medicine, parts, steel. Nobody gave an order. A clan that has never won anything heard that one finally had.
They want to dig here, and to stand here the next time the sky opens.
Accept: two Reds join the colony, and the supplies come down beside it. Refuse: they go home with their pod. The story continues either way.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_HouseText:
A factor of {0} has arrived with a contract and no visible opinion about the war.
The Society's tithe-men no longer collect here, which means the helium under your claim currently belongs to nobody the markets recognise. {0} would like to be first in the queue. They offer open trade and their goodwill, and a caravan is already waiting over the ridge in case you say yes.
The Sons of Ares will not like it. They do not trust anyone who can count that fast.
Accept: {0} thinks better of you and sends a trade caravan now. The Sons of Ares think slightly less of you. Refuse: the factor leaves. The story continues either way.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_PriceText:
The Society has stopped sending armies. It has started sending a number.
There is now a standing price on {PAWN_nameDef}, payable to any Lurcher who brings back the hand with the Red sigil on it. No more ships will come for the claim. Hunters will come for {PAWN_objective}, and keep coming, for exactly as long as that hand says Red and that body says Gold.
It is the mismatch they are paid for. A Violet with a steady hand could rewrite the mark so the paper and the body agree - "forge a sigil", on an operating table - and the hunters would have nothing left to look for.
Until then, expect Lurchers.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_EndingText:
The fighting has stopped for long enough that people have started asking what it was for.
Messengers are waiting on an answer, and they will not wait much longer.
The Sons of Ares want the claim as an open ally: a place on the map where the Rising is not hiding. It would mean their friendship, and it would mean never being let alone by the Society again.
The Rim Dominion has sent an envoy too. Its Golds are no kinder than the Society's, only further away and at odds with them. They offer their protection and their friendship. The Sons of Ares would not forgive it.
Or the claim can belong to nobody. A clan that digs its own helium and answers to no Color at all - which has not existed anywhere for eight hundred years.
Belong to nobody: nothing changes. Stand with the Sons of Ares: they become your allies. Take the Rim Dominion's hand: it becomes your ally, and the Sons of Ares think much less of you.
Whichever you choose, the claim will have to live with it.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_Option_ares: Stand with the Sons of Ares
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_End_free:
The messengers were sent home with the same answer.
No banner goes up over the rig. No sigil is painted on the gate. The clan digs, and what it digs is its own, and when someone asks whose claim this is the answer is a list of first names.
It may not last. Nothing like it has, yet.
For now, the claim is quiet.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_End_ares:
The answer went back to the Sons of Ares the same night: yes, and openly.
They are your allies now. Their people will come when you call and trade when you ask, and the Society will never again mistake this claim for a mining clan with a grievance. It is a piece of the Rising with a map reference.
That was always the risk. It was also always the point.
For now, the claim is quiet.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_End_dominion:
The Dominion's envoy bowed, a little, which Golds do not do to Reds, and left with the claim's answer.
The Rim Dominion is your ally now, and its ships are a thing the Society must think about before it thinks about you. The Sons of Ares have been told. Their reply was one word and it was not a kind one.
The clan has a protector. It has not yet learned what protectors cost.
For now, the claim is quiet.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_QuietText:
No more word comes.
The roads are quiet and the sky is empty. Whatever the Society means to do about the claim, it is not doing it this season.
The story told here is finished. The colony is yours, for as long as you can keep it.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_DepotText:
A runner from {0} has brought a map with one mark on it.
Every canister the tithe-men ever took from this district went to the same place first: a depot a few days' travel from the claim, where the helium waits for the ships. Yours is in it. So is every other clan's.
Since the Rain it is held by what the garrison had left. That will not stay true. In about {1} days the next ship comes, the stacks go up to orbit, and the guard is doubled.
Until now the Society has always come to you.
Accept: the depot is marked on the world map. Send a caravan and take it within {1} days. Refuse: the story ends here. Your colony plays on as an ordinary one.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_DepotMarkedText:
The depot is marked on the world map. It is a Society outpost: walls, a garrison, and the district's helium stacked inside.
Form a caravan and attack it. Kill or drive off everyone holding it. You have about {0} days before the ship comes for the stacks.
Leave enough people behind to hold the claim. The Society has not stopped looking at it.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_DepotRefusedText:
The runner folded the map and took it away again.
It was a great deal to ask of a clan that has already been asked for everything. The helium will go up to the ships as it always has, and the claim will go on being a place that survived.
The story told here is finished. The colony is yours, for as long as you can keep it.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_DepotLostText:
The ship came for the stacks.
The depot is empty now, and the helium that was in it is somewhere above the sky. There will be another quarter and another tithe, somewhere, from someone. The chance to take this one back has gone.
The story told here is finished. The colony is yours, for as long as you can keep it.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_DepotTakenText:
The last of the guard is down, and the stacks are still here.
Row on row of canisters, each stencilled with the mark of the clan it was taken from. Some of the marks are yours. Most belong to clans who will find out, in the next few days, that a tithe can be taken back.
{0} canisters are on their way to the claim by pod. The rest is going home to whoever dug it.
Bring your people back. Nobody takes a Gold's helium and is left to enjoy it.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_PraetorText:
They have not sent Grays this time.
A Praetor has come down in person, with peers at the shoulder and Obsidians at the back. Golds do not do this for a mining clan. They do it when the alternative is explaining, to other Golds, how a mining clan emptied a depot.
These are the people the whole hierarchy exists to produce. Everything below them was built so that this fight would never have to happen.
It is happening.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_TermsText:
A White has come under a flag of truce, alone, carrying a ledger.
The Society does not surrender, and this is not a surrender. It is an entry. The claim is to be recorded as exhausted: seam dry, clan dispersed, nothing of value remaining. Nobody is sent to an exhausted claim. No tithe-men, no garrison, no hunters. On paper, you would stop existing, and in practice you would be left alone.
All it needs is that you let the entry stand.
The Sons of Ares have already said what they think of a Rising that signs the Society's books.
Let the ledger stand: the Society becomes neutral. With no war, the Lurchers stop coming. The Sons of Ares think much less of you. Burn the ledger: the war goes on. The Sons of Ares think more of you.
Whichever you choose ends the story told here.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_Terms_truce:
The White closed the ledger and went back down the road.
Somewhere a clerk has written that this ground is finished, and for the first time in eight hundred years a lie in the Society's books is working in a Red's favour. The rig is running. The seam is nowhere near dry. Officially, nobody is here to see it.
It is a quiet kind of freedom, and it was bought with a signature the Sons of Ares will not forget.
The story told here is finished. The colony is yours, for as long as you can keep it.
LanguageData.RR_Campaign_Terms_burn:
The ledger burned well. The White watched it go and said nothing, which Whites are trained to do.
There will be no entry. The claim stays on the Society's maps as what it is: a place where the hierarchy was told no, and then told no again by people it had already sent Golds to kill.
They will be back. They know where you are. So, now, does everyone else.
The story told here is finished. The colony is yours, for as long as you can keep it.
